clue.text: Begin with the outstanding aristocrat

parts.note: an outstanding performer is a star
a toff is British slang for a posh upper-class person

explanation.surface: Advice to open proceedings with the most distinguished nobleman present.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is a phrasal verb for commencing something.

clue.text: Leave the main stream before the Dee turns dry?

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: turns means changes round, so the letters of Dee are rearranged

explanation.surface: A river wonders whether to leave the main flow before the Dee runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges DEE to EDE. The Dee is a British river, which makes 'main stream' look like water.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to break away from a larger body such as a federation or church.

clue.text: O for a pill to treat a spring sucker

indicators.note: to treat means to process or work on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A plea for a pill to treat someone who gets caught out in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a coiled spring or season of health; it is the first of April.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked by a prank on the first of April is the gullible victim of the day.

clue.text: Incredibly lucky, in toto: do nothing: go back to gamble and regret will follow

indicators.note: will follow means this piece comes after the others
in means the reversed piece is placed within the letters of toto
go back means the run of letters is read in reverse order

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
to bet is to gamble
rue means regret

explanation.surface: Advice to someone on a lucky streak: stop, retreat from gambling, or you will regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is long and chatty, but 'in' is a container signal and 'go back' a reversal, both acting on short words; 'will follow' sets the gamble and regret at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too good to be true is suspiciously fortunate, almost beyond belief.

clue.text: Dandified drinker absorbing work for piano

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking up, so the drinker takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: to drink like a fish, so a fish is a heavy drinker
op is short for opus, a musical work
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A foppish drinker soaks up a piece written for piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'drinks like a fish' makes a fish a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Foppish describes a man who is overly concerned with fashionable clothes, like a dandy.

clue.text: A teacher's lost his heart to a plant

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letter of the teacher's word drops out

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher; with the 's that gives rabbis

explanation.surface: A teacher has fallen in love with a plant, losing his heart to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his heart' reads like romance, but it is a deletion signal removing a middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabis, or rock cress, is a genus of low flowering garden plants.

clue.text: Creator of sleuth rendered on my card as man with dog

indicators.note: rendered means made into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a handler is someone who works with a dog, for example a police dog

explanation.surface: A writer of detective stories appears on someone's card portrayed with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges ON MY CARD to RAYMOND C.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe detective novels such as The Big Sleep.

clue.text: The second Elizabeth retains time of sudden attack

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: retains means holds onto, so the name keeps the time letter within

parts.note: Liz is a short form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth II holds on through a time of sudden bombing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The second Elizabeth' looks like Queen Elizabeth II; it is B (second letter) and LIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is an intense, sudden military attack, especially by air.

clue.text: Holy wizard losing his head over good British money

parts.note: St is short for saint, a holy person

indicators.note: losing his head means the wizard's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend

explanation.surface: A holy wizard goes off his head over a pile of good British cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' removes the M of MERLIN, leaving ERLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling is the currency of the United Kingdom, the pound.

clue.text: Fitted up like a picture

definitions.meaning: falsely incriminated, set up to take the blame
mounted with a border, as a painting is

explanation.surface: A man wrongly accused, displayed like a painting on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang sense is falsely incriminated, and the literal sense is set in a border like artwork.

clue.text: Petrol makes the load

parts.note: fuel is what makes a motor vehicle run

explanation.surface: A remark that fuel turns out to be the burden being carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Petrol makes the car go: split the answer into two words to see the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is freight, the goods carried by a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Shared communication along loyalists' toes?

definitions.meaning: a telephone connection shared by several subscribers
loyal members are said to toe the official policy of their political group

explanation.surface: A shared phone link imagined as the line that loyalists keep their toes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed phrases: an old shared telephone circuit, and the official policy members must toe.

clue.text: Other minds, including singer, have trouble distinguishing signals

indicators.note: including means the singer goes inside the rearranged letters
other means a different form, so the letters of minds are rearranged

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: People of different minds, a singer among them, struggle to tell signals apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' signals an anagram, and 'including' wraps that around the singer. John Dalton, the chemist, described his own colour blindness, hence the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daltonism is colour blindness, which makes red and green traffic or railway signals hard to tell apart.

clue.text: Greek spirit diminished by the Spanish bird

indicators.note: diminished means cut short, so the drink loses its final letter

parts.note: ouzo is an aniseed-flavoured Greek spirit
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Greek drink is watered down by a Spanish bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished' drops the last O of OUZO, leaving OUZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The ouzel, or ring ouzel, is a thrush-like blackbird.

clue.text: Who had problems with seat on a Jumbo?

indicators.note: having problems suggests the words are in disorder and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A question about who ran into difficulty with the seats on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jumbo jet, but it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat carried on an elephant's back.

clue.text: Begetter of Alice and also (thank God) a boy

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again
DG stands for Dei gratia, Latin for by the grace of God, as on British coins
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: The creator of Alice is also, thankfully, a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: D.G. (Dei gratia) appears on British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge Dodgson wrote the Alice books under the pen name Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Astonished by Spurs' dire performance

indicators.note: a dire performance suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan is shocked by how badly Tottenham Hotspur played.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club; 'dire' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprised means taken aback, startled by something unexpected.

clue.text: Bottom's up after lady dramatist

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the lady in the answer

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a lady

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point, the bottom

explanation.surface: Bottom from A Midsummer Night's Dream stands up after a lady in a playwright's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NADIR to RIDAN in this down clue. 'Bottom' suggests Shakespeare's weaver, apt for a dramatist clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was the Irish playwright of The School for Scandal and The Rivals.

clue.text: Wine keeps the sick in slight elevation

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside the wine

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine
the sick are those who are ill

explanation.surface: Wine keeps patients' spirits slightly raised.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British name for German white Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillock is a small hill, a gentle rise in the ground.

clue.text: Little beast's equipment number

definitions.note: the 's reads as is, joining the young animal to its wordplay

parts.note: kit means equipment
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A small animal's gear is given a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, a small animal.

clue.text: Runner entertaining lady means to be compatible

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the runner's name takes the lady inside it

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is a famous British middle-distance runner
her is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: An athlete who entertains a woman means to get along with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests a generic athlete, but it is Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic champion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together or be consistent, as compatible things are.

clue.text: Put Laurel in the England team: this could wind one up

parts.note: to cap a player is to put them in the national side
Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A call to pick Stan Laurel for England, which would surely annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind one up' suggests annoyance; a capstan is a revolving drum used to wind in rope or cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a vertical winch on a ship, turned to haul in cables.

clue.text: Not just dark?

definitions.meaning: dark-haired, read as the opposite of fair-haired

explanation.surface: A question whether darkness is simply an injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means both just and light-haired, so the negative covers unjust and, whimsically, dark.

clue.text: Ransack with shooter

definitions.meaning: to search thoroughly and roughly, plundering as you go

explanation.surface: A burglar ransacking a house while armed with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to rummage and plunder, and the noun sense is a long gun fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: See 26 across
Game with mashed turnip dressing

indicators.note: dressing means clothing, so the scrambled letters wrap around the other piece
mashed means pulped, so the letters of turnip are scrambled

parts.note: and means with, both joining things together

explanation.surface: A dish of mashed turnip served with dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed' is the anagram signal and 'dressing' wraps the result round 'with'. Tip and run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip and run is an informal version of cricket played as a game.

clue.text: Chap taking the plunge going a different way

parts.note: a diver is someone who plunges into water
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A man who takes the plunge and heads off in another direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent describes lines or paths that branch apart from one another.

clue.text: Surrounded by seaweeds -secure from disease

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Surrounded by seaweeds -secure from disease' for LASSA FEVER: LAVER around SAFE gives LASAFEVER, one S short, and nothing in the clue as held supplies the second S.

clue.text: Audacity's a psychological problem

definitions.meaning: audacity is nerve, and the 's makes it ..., read as nerve is
anxiety or tension, as in a bout of the jitters

explanation.surface: Someone's boldness is in fact a sign of a mental disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is cheek or boldness, while having nerves means suffering from anxiety.

clue.text: He barges in rattling a tin -not so polite

indicators.note: rattling means shaking about, so the letters of tin are jumbled

parts.note: ruder means less polite

explanation.surface: A man bursts in shaking a collecting tin, with manners worse than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattling' signals an anagram of only the short word before the dash; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who barges in uninvited is an interloper who enters without permission.
